title: Canonical Vehicle-Owner Master Data Service (vehicle-registry-canonical-record)

# Canonical Vehicle-Owner Master Data Service (vehicle-registry-canonical-record)

## Problem & How Truth Is Established Today
Vehicle-owner truth in Indonesia is split across three agencies with no single canonical master: **Korlantas Polri** (Ditregident) issues and holds BPKB/STNK records, run through its Electronic Registration and Identification (ERI) system, launched 2017 to integrate BPKB/STNK data across regions; **provincial Bapenda** offices hold the tax-collection (PKB) record via Samsat and the national SIGNAL app; **PT Jasa Raharja** (state-owned) holds the SWDKLLJ accident-insurance owner record used for compensation. These three records are reconciled manually and imperfectly at Samsat one-stop counters; no independently verified cross-agency master exists.

## Buyer & Who Pays
Two possible buyer framings: (1) **State agencies** (Korlantas, Bapenda, Jasa Raharja) themselves — but this is a single, government-procurement sale requiring negotiation with three separate sovereign bodies, which is an enterprise/government-sales motion. (2) **Private-sector risk buyers** — vehicle insurers (underwriting/TLO), multifinance/leasing companies (collateral and default risk), and used-vehicle marketplaces (buyer protection) — who want a reconciled, trustworthy owner/status record. In practice, these private buyers today rely only on each agency's own already-public lookup (provincial Samsat portals, SIGNAL), not a privileged cross-agency reconciliation — because no such privileged access is obtainable by a private company.

## Documented Failures (cited)
- **Compliance gap**: at Rakornas Samsat 2026 (Bandar Lampung, 14 Jul 2026), data through June 2026 showed 51.9 million vehicles past their PKB due date; only ~24 million (46.28%) paid, leaving ~27 million non-compliant (Kompas Otomotif, 21 Jul 2026, reporting the Rakornas). Jasa Raharja Director-General Muhammad Awaluddin explicitly named cross-agency data integration as the fix still needed: "Transformasi pelayanan Samsat harus berorientasi pada integrasi data... menghubungkan informasi lintas instansi" (Kompas Otomotif; multiple regional outlets, 15–27 Jul 2026).
- **Document fraud**: Polda Kalimantan Selatan (Feb 2026) dismantled a cross-provincial STNK/BPKB forgery syndicate spanning Central Java, West Java, East Java, Yogyakarta, Bali, and Kalimantan — ~20,000 forged document sheets and ~20 counterfeit vehicles seized, with monthly profits of ~Rp100 million from forged BPKB/STNK plus ~Rp20.8M from forged tax notices (Detik Kalimantan, 19 Feb 2026; Kalseltoday, Feb 2026).
- **System reliability**: SIGNAL (the national digital Samsat app) has recurring failures traced to stale/un-synced Bapenda data — users cannot get tax figures because "data kendaraan yang dimasukkan belum update di Bapenda" (Kompas Otomotif, Dec 2025).

## Bottom-Up ARR Path
Weak on both framings. Government-buyer path fails K4 outright (single enterprise/political sale, not self-serve). Private-sector path is undermined by K1: any product a private company could build is limited to re-aggregating each agency's own already-public lookup (Samsat portals, SIGNAL) — commodity data any competitor can also pull — not a privileged reconciliation of the conflicting agency databases. No named Indonesian company was found paying specifically for cross-agency reconciliation (as opposed to single-agency lookup, which MATEL already provides for leasing default-checking). No credible count × ACV path to $1M ARR was constructed.

## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)
**ERI (Electronic Registration and Identification)** — Korlantas Polri's own national vehicle-registration database, mandatory for all Bapenda/Samsat offices, running since 2017 (jlp.puslitbang.polri.go.id; korlantas.polri.go.id), built to integrate BPKB/STNK data and provide unified registration-history access. **Samsat Digital Nasional (SIGNAL)** — the tri-agency (Kemendagri/Korlantas/Jasa Raharja) national app for tax payment and STNK validation (samsatdigital.id). **Bilateral integration pilots** — e.g., Korlantas–Bapenda Kaltara (korlantas.polri.go.id). **Mata Elang (MATEL)** — a private app used by leasing/debt-collection agencies to check plate-number arrears status — the closest private analog, but scoped to leasing-default checking, not cross-agency canonical reconciliation.

## Kill Tests
- **K1 (Data access) — FAIL.** The contested truth (which agency's record is correct) requires cooperation from the very agencies whose records disagree (Korlantas, Bapenda, Jasa Raharja); a private company has no legal or contractual standing to arbitrate between three sovereign data holders, only to re-publish what each already exposes publicly. This mirrors the previously validated Program A pattern (fisheries multiagency, carbon interministry, one-map overlap): inter-ministerial data conflicts are not privately resolvable.
- **K2 (Oracle bound) — PASS.** In isolation, "who is the correct current owner" is a records-reconciliation/entity-resolution problem, inferable from the underlying agency databases if access existed — not a fabricated-at-source physical truth.
- **K3 (Absorption) — FAIL.** Korlantas's ERI system is a funded, nationally mandated program (since 2017, mandatory for all Bapenda/Samsat) targeting exactly this canonical integration function; the July 2026 Rakornas Samsat reaffirmed cross-agency data integration as the National Samsat Supervisory Board's stated current priority, with Jasa Raharja's own Director-General publicly calling for it. This is cited evidence of an active, ongoing 12-month absorption effort by the incumbent state system, not mere "could build it" speculation.
- **K4 (Bootstrap bar) — FAIL.** No self-serve/API path to $1M ARR survives K1: the government-buyer version requires enterprise/political sales (excluded by G6); the private-buyer version is confined to commodity public-lookup data with no evidenced paying customer base beyond adjacent tools (MATEL) already serving a narrower need.

## Scores
- Severity 7 — 27M non-compliant vehicles and a documented cross-provincial forgery syndicate are real, recurring, agency-managed losses (Rakornas Samsat 2026; Polda Kalsel Feb 2026).
- Revenue 3 — no credible customer/ACV path survives the K1 constraint.
- WTP 5 — the state clearly has budget and is actively pursuing integration, but this budget is not privately reachable.
- Data 3 — any private product is confined to commodity data already public via provincial Samsat portals.
- Absorption 3 — Korlantas's ERI plus the 2026 Rakornas reaffirmation is direct, cited incumbent activity in the exact function.
- Competition 3 — funded, mandatory state incumbent (ERI/SIGNAL) already has nationwide traction; MATEL covers the closest private niche.
- Moat 3 — a commodity-data reseller has no defensible position.
- **Weighted: 4.1**

## Upside Flag
Secondary evidence only: if OJK or Korlantas ever opened a sanctioned data-sharing sandbox (an "open Samsat" API akin to open-banking initiatives) granting licensed private analytics vendors read access across agencies, a reconciliation layer could re-enter as viable — no evidence this exists or is planned was found as of mid-2026.

## What Would Kill This
Already killed on K1 and K3: the underlying data conflict is inter-agency and the incumbent (Korlantas via ERI, reaffirmed at Rakornas Samsat 2026) is the active owner of exactly this integration effort. Revival would require either a licensed private-sector data-sharing mandate from Korlantas/Bapenda/Jasa Raharja, or clear evidence ERI's mandate has stalled/been defunded — neither found.
